title: What I changed in Change Stack
intro: I kept the layer-based review model and focused on staying oriented while checking an explanation against code. The original already has summary navigation and explicit viewed status. I changed their presentation and added a return path for one cross-file inspection.
rows: File identity and controls compete with the code.
The file list stays available in the rail. A fixed layer switcher keeps all seven layers reachable when files are expanded. Outline sits beside the code; occasional file actions stay in Tools.
A broad summary range leaves the supporting statement to find.

Six compact rows pair each statement with its code range. Full wording stays available. Inspect guard opens feedback-access.ts; Return restores the caller. About links explains that these manually mapped ranges are starting points, not proof.
File context and layer context need different scopes.

This file shows the selected explanation. Entire layer starts with compact summary rows across the nine paths. Scope and tabs stay fixed while context scrolls. Coverage is explicit: 14 of 37 summaries captured.
File viewed, summary seen and PR status mean different things.

Included files counts seven captured diffs. The layer shows seven reviewable files and two unavailable patches. Opening a file marks nothing viewed. Mark viewed has Undo. Summary seen stays in Summary options. The merged snapshot disables Submit review.
tradeoff: Wrapped 13 px code trades horizontal movement for vertical scrolling. Added-file Split uses a 96 px Before rail; Equal panes restores 50/50. A direct anchor is a starting point: surrounding code and the complete source summary stay available.
validation: I checked direct code links, guard/return navigation, context scopes, progress and Undo, notes, Copy path, the six entities and keyboard access. The 1440 px, 1280 px and 1100 px layouts passed. These are implementation checks; developer testing remains outstanding.
scope: Formbricks #8650 at the out-of-date 23cdac2 snapshot. Seven of 52 diffs are included. The comparison uses final M with the same imports and six source points; the original capture is untouched. Full file and Captured ranges do not recreate semantic diffs. Nothing is sent.
next: I’d test the caller, guard and return task, then start from code and ask what could make a reviewer disagree with the summary. Compare explanation accuracy and wrong turns on the same commit. Modified-file review and stale anchors still need testing.
